title: Sonny and the Dingo Pup | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka spots a young dingo pup playing completely alone in a moonlit clearing — chasing its own tail, pouncing on shadows, unbothered by anything — and feels the pure joy of it from all the way across the clearing. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
There was a pup in the clearing.

A dingo pup — young, sandy-gold, with a white-tipped tail and large pale paws it hadn't quite grown into yet. It was alone, and it was playing.

Not playing with anything in particular. Just playing. It chased its tail twice, caught it the second time, then looked surprised. It pounced on a shadow. It found a stick, worried it for a moment, then dropped it and forgot it entirely. It galloped in a small circle for no reason.

Sunny watched from the treeline, smiling so wide her cheeks hurt.

The pup had no idea it was being watched, or if it did, it didn't care. It had important things to do, such as pouncing and galloping and chasing its own tail.

It stopped in the centre of the clearing, panting slightly, and looked around at the bush. Then it sat down in the moonlight with the comfortable abruptness of a creature that has decided this is exactly where it will be now.

Sunny thought: there is nothing better in the whole world than that.

The pup shook its head, scratched one ear, then lay down flat in the grass, chin on the ground, eyes closing.

All that energy. All at once. Gone.

Sunny lay down too, still smiling.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, dingo pup. Goodnight, little one.
